moduleTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models
title: Cloud Computing — Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Assessment
description: Checkpoint evaluation verifying conceptual mastery across Cloud Architecture, Regions & Service Models (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) and Elastic Compute, Containers & Serverless Workloads.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: In the Cloud Shared Responsibility Model for an IaaS virtual machine (e.g., AWS EC2), who is responsible for applying Linux security patches inside the VM?

options.text: The customer
The cloud hardware provider
The DNS registrar
Patches are unnecessary in virtual machines

questions.explanation: In IaaS, the customer owns the guest OS, installed packages, firewall Security Groups, and application data.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why do resilient architectures span at least two Availability Zones within a Region?

options.text: To survive a single physical data center power, cooling, or fiber failure with minimal latency
Because single-AZ regions refuse HTTPS TLS certificates
To avoid creating any VPC subnets
To bypass IAM authentication

questions.explanation: Availability Zones are physically isolated facilities inside a region designed for fault containment.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Which service model lets developers push pure function handlers triggered by HTTP/events without managing servers or OS upgrades?

options.text: Serverless / FaaS (PaaS tier)
Bare-Metal Colocation
Raw Physical Hypervisor
Static IaaS VM

questions.explanation: Serverless Function-as-a-Service automates server provisioning, scaling, and runtime OS patching.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: What happens if an auto-scaled web server saves uploaded user avatars onto its local EC2 instance disk?

options.text: Files vanish when instances scale down or get replaced, and other balanced instances cannot serve those files
Cloud providers sync `/var/uploads` globally automatically
Docker copies files across regions in 1ms
Load balancers store binary files inside headers

questions.explanation: Local disks on auto-scaled nodes are ephemeral and node-bound; durable shared assets belong in Object Storage (S3/GCS).

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: Why do multi-stage Dockerfiles produce cleaner, safer cloud images?

options.text: Compilers and dev caches stay isolated in the build stage and are omitted from the lean runtime container
They allow root SSH access directly from browsers
They skip TLS verification on registries
They bundle entire VM hypervisors inside containers

questions.explanation: Smaller runtime images transfer faster across clusters and reduce exposed software CVEs.

questions.sectionTitle: Module 1: Cloud Architecture & Core Service Models Checkpoint
questions.prompt: When is a Serverless function (Lambda / Cloud Functions) generally LESS appropriate than containers/VMs?

options.text: Sustained CPU-saturated rendering jobs running continuously for hours or requiring persistent raw WebSockets
Asynchronous thumbnail generation on S3 image upload
Low-traffic webhook receivers
Scheduled nightly cleanup cron jobs

questions.explanation: Continuous compute-saturated workloads and persistent long-lived stateful protocols are often cheaper and better served on containers/VMs.
